Restricted funding is money that comes with rules. The funder says what it can be spent on, such as one program, one group of people, or one time period. You must use it for that purpose.

Flexible funding is also called unrestricted or general operating support. Your team can use it where the need is greatest, such as supervision, data work or training.

Your report says most of your money is restricted government funding. That is why it helps to know which grants are confirmed, what each one can pay for, and when each one ends. Asking a few funders for some flexible support is a good next step. The funding guide on ARCvi can help you think it through.

Both steps are high priorities in your report, and both are small enough to start now.

The first is seeing your funding for the next year (FR7). About 80% of your money is restricted government funding, so it is hard to tell what is confirmed and what is still pending. A 12-month funding map shows you where money could run short before it does. That helps you protect your hospital and street outreach staff.

The second is training everyone to collect data the same way (ML6). Your team already uses standard tools and reviews data together. But not everyone has been trained on the same rules. Until the data is consistent, it is hard to trust it or build on it. Clean data also helps you move past counting activity to showing real change.

These two steps support each other, and they make your later funding conversations stronger.
